# `bill_subjects`

One row per congressional bill that a subject carrier has answered for, built by `enrich_bill_subjects`. This is the per-bill detail pass `congress_bills` deliberately omits: the `/bill` list payload carries no subject signal at all, so the Library of Congress assignment — one `policy_area` from a ~33-term controlled list, plus any number of legislative subjects from a large controlled vocabulary — is fetched one bill at a time and published here. Keyed by `bill_id`, so it joins straight to `congress_bills` with a `LEFT JOIN`. The enrichment is bounded and resumable: each run answers for a capped slice of the archive and merges with the prior table, so coverage grows run over run and is always partial by design. A row with a null `policy_area` records that the named carrier was asked and had nothing, not that the fetch failed — failed fetches write no row. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.

- **Parquet file:** `bill_subjects.parquet`
- **Queryable via MCP `query_sql`:** Yes

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bill_id` | `VARCHAR` | Synthetic bill key `{congress}-{type}-{number}` (e.g. `118-hr-1234`). Primary key / dedup key, and the join key to `congress_bills.bill_id`. |
| `policy_area` | `VARCHAR` | The bill's single Library of Congress policy area (e.g. `Health`, `Armed Forces and National Security`), from a controlled list of ~33 terms. Null when the carrier holds no assignment for the bill. |
| `subjects_json` | `VARCHAR` | JSON array of the bill's legislative subject terms (a large controlled vocabulary), in the order the carrier returned them, deduplicated. `[]` when none are assigned. |
| `subject_count` | `VARCHAR` | Number of terms in `subjects_json`, so a count query needs no JSON parsing. |
| `carrier` | `VARCHAR` | Which publisher supplied the row: `congress-api` (Congress.gov v3 `/bill/{congress}/{type}/{number}/subjects`, back to the 93rd Congress, needs an api.data.gov key) or `govinfo-billstatus` (GPO BILLSTATUS bulk data, keyless, back to the 108th Congress). The terms are identical strings; only the carrier differs. |
| `enriched_at` | `VARCHAR` | UTC ISO 8601 timestamp of the run that fetched this row. |
